subject.title: Add Gee runtime ownership envelope for OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw core add a generic external-host ownership contract, or should Gee remain outside core behind existing plugin and runtime seams?
rationale: The PR adds a named external host owner across core auth, tools, compaction, failover, and persisted Codex bindings, while current architecture and repository policy define runtimes and plugins as the ownership boundaries.

options.title: Design a generic host contract
options.body: Sponsor an owner-neutral API for prepared facts and ephemeral credential, tool, and compaction resolvers, then implement Gee-specific policy in its owner integration.

options.title: Approve Gee in core
options.body: Accept Gee as a first-class core owner and require a complete auth resolver, documented activation, migration contract, and live end-to-end proof.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Close the PR and keep host-specific orchestration in the external owner integration using existing supported seams.

recommendation.title: Design a generic host contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor an owner-neutral API for prepared facts and ephemeral credential, tool, and compaction resolvers, then implement Gee-specific policy in its owner integration.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to the runtime architecture and current auth-routing contract that the proposed external-host boundary would change.
